threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You ask for a ‘cuppa’ at a café and get a confused look. It's tea, mate, not a trendy new drink.
Last night, on the 59, a guy serenaded us with old school raps while trying to sell a broken phone. Best night bus entertainment I've had in ages.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a street musician serenading a cat in a sunbeam outside my window—only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a spontaneous parade of cyclists celebrating a random Tuesday. It's like a local holiday no one else knows about!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they navigate BART delays—total calm, casually checking their phone while others panic. It's an art.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 Balboa yesterday. A guy was busting out opera while we waited 20 mins. Bravo to him, but I just wanted to get home!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the lively plazas are for festivals. In reality, locals use them for quiet chats and siestas, not just celebrations.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still asking for a ‘taxi’ instead of ‘cab’ and looking up how to pronounce ‘Sagrada Família’ as they walk past it.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think you can get a seat on the tube during rush hour—bless your heart, mate. That’s when the real Londoners stand.
Caught a lad on the 35 bragging about how he ‘broke the tube strike’ by cycling all the way to Borough. Said it was like a scene from a movie.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: One night I saw a group of teens setting up a pop-up cinema in the park, complete with fairy lights and blankets. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can spot the spontaneous techno parties in hidden courtyards. Beats drop, people dance, and it feels like you stumbled into another world.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know the best alleyways for murals and the unmarked taco trucks that get the late-night crowd buzzing.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a tourist trying to explain how to catch a Muni bus to a local. The local just shrugged, smirked, and kept walking. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but it's the hidden calles that show true local life—where the real magic happens.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their confusion at the refuse collection schedule—only locals know it shifts for holidays.
